detailZh: 梅赛德斯确认安东内利和拉塞尔将驾驶最新规格赛车参加本周末的美国大奖赛。
在新加坡大奖赛中，安东内利驾驶了车队在马来西亚的升级版赛车，而拉塞尔则回归到旧规格。
安东内利有可能在美国大奖赛中赢得2026年的车手冠军。
克雷格·斯莱特解释了安东内利如何在周末的美国大奖赛中赢得F1世界冠军。
车队期待已久的全新空气动力学套件在本月初F1重返马来西亚时表现不佳，只有安东内利在新加坡的比赛中使用了升级套件，而拉塞尔因为主场比赛的网格处罚，在那个周末回归到赛帕ング版本，以便车队可以在赛道上比较两种套件。
安东内利在新加坡的冲刺周末起步时比拉塞尔落后，但随着比赛的进行，他的竞争力有所提升，并在比赛中获得第三名，沃尔夫赛后表示，车队倾向于在奥斯汀使用两辆新规格的赛车。

梅赛德斯车队负责人现在在车队赛事预告中确认了该计划，在即将到来的比赛周末，安东内利可能赢得世界冠军。
"马来西亚和新加坡对我们来说是艰难的周末，我们努力去理解我们哪里做得不够好，"沃尔夫说。
"奥斯汀给了我们回应的机会。我们将继续开发赛车，在两辆车上使用我们最新的升级套件。"
"由于赛道非常接近，如果我们想在赛季末段持续保持在前端竞争，我们就需要继续前进。"
"乔治·拉塞尔在新加坡的冲刺赛雨中延迟期间接替了基米·安东内利的工程师职位。"
"尽管在马来西亚和新加坡的比赛中没有挑战胜利，但随着马克斯·维斯塔潘连续赢得胜利，红牛车队强势复苏，梅赛德斯车队仍然坚定地朝着今年获得世界冠军双冠的目标前进，目前赛季还剩下六轮。"
安东内利如果在周日赢得比赛，而队友拉塞尔未能进入前八名，且法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿不在前四名，他最早将在本周日赢得他的首个车手总冠军。
与此同时，梅赛德斯在车队总冠军中领先法拉利134分，这意味着银箭车队最早可能在下周的墨西哥城大奖赛中获得冠军。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳开玩笑说，没有他在F1中，托托·沃尔夫的生活要容易得多，回顾他们多年来激烈的竞争。
沃尔夫表示，他的车队将继续一步一个脚印地前进。
"美国大奖赛开始了又一轮要求严格的连续三站赛事，"沃尔夫补充道。
"有很多事情要做，但我们不会急于求成。我们的首要任务是面前的周末：出色地执行，最大化我们的表现，并且对每一场比赛都做好应对。"
梅赛德斯在奥斯汀将第三次在比赛中使用改进的车身涂装，蓝色被添加到W17s上，以突出汽车公司的MANUFAKTUR个性化项目。

detailEn: Mercedes confirm Kimi Antonelli. George Russell to both run latest Mercedes car upgrades at United States GP

Kimi Antonelli ran the team's Malaysia upgrades, while George Russell reverted to the older specification, in Singapore; Antonelli could clinch 2026 drivers' title in the USA; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin from Friday evening, live on Sky Sports F1
Craig Slater explains how Kimi Antonelli can clinch the F1 world title this weekend at the United States Grand Prix.
Mercedes have confirmed Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will both run their latest-specification car at this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

After a problematic debut for the team's long-awaited new aerodynamic package on F1's return to Malaysia earlier this month, only Antonelli ran the upgrades last time out in Singapore while Russell, who carried a grid penalty for the main race into that weekend, reverting to the pre-Sepang version so the team could compare the two on track.

Antonelli had started the Sprint weekend in Singapore on the back foot compared to Russell but his competitiveness improved as the event progressed and he finished third in the race, with Wolff suggesting afterwards that the team were leaning towards running both cars with the new specification in Austin.

The Mercedes team principal has now confirmed that plan in the team's event preview ahead of a race weekend that Antonelli could clinch the world title.
"Malaysia and Singapore were difficult weekends for us and we have worked hard to understand where we fell short," said Wolff.
"Austin gives us an opportunity to respond. We will run our latest update package on both cars as we continue to develop the car.
"The field is incredibly close, so we need to keep moving forward if we want to fight consistently at the front in the closing stages of the season."
George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

Despite not challenging for victory in either Malaysia or Singapore, with Max Verstappen taking back-to-back wins for a resurgent Red Bull, Mercedes remain firmly on course to secure a world championship double this year with six rounds of the season left.

Antonelli would clinch his maiden Drivers' Championship as earlier as this Sunday if he wins and team-mate Russell fails to finish in the top eight and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton is not in the top four.

Mercedes' 134-point lead over Ferrari at the top of the Constructors' Championship, meanwhile, means the Silver Arrows could be in a title-winning position for that title as early as next week's Mexico City Grand Prix.
Christian Horner jokes that Toto Wolff's life is much easier without him in F1, reflecting on their fierce rivalry over the years.
Wolff says his team will continue to take things one step at a time.
"The United States Grand Prix begins another demanding triple-header," added Wolff.
"There is plenty at stake, but we won't get ahead of ourselves. The priority is the weekend in front of us: execute well, maximise our performance and take each race as it comes."
Mercedes will run a revised livery for the second time in three races in Austin, with blue added to the W17s to highlight the car company's MANUFAKTUR personalisation programme.

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
